text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO breach detected for customer Rivermark (single-tenant, eu-west-1). p95 and p99 have spiked starting 2024-03-06T12:07:00Z. p95=1.2s (baseline 0.18s), p99=11.4s (baseline 0.55s). Streaming stalls and aborted sessions observed. Incident ID: INC-7832. Please acknowledge.

samir: acked. I'm oncall. assigning triage. who saw the first alerts?

maya: saw grafana spike at 12:06:30, matched with surge in active sessions for rivermark-org (concurrency x3 usual). link: https://grafana.example.com/d/ABC/rivermark-latency?from=now-15m

lee: quick metrics dump I ran:
```
# top-level aggregates (eu-west-1, rivermark)
p50: 0.12s
p95: 1.20s
p99: 11.4s
streaming stall rate: 8.3% (normal <0.5%)
active sessions: 642 (baseline 210)
request pattern: many long-prefix prompts, median prompt tokens 420 -> 2300 in spike
```

joan: logs show repeated KV cache evictions + prefix mismatch churn. snippet from inference-runtime logs (pod inference-rr-7f8):
```
2024-03-06T12:06:40Z WARN kv_cache: eviction triggered: reason=fragmentation keys_evicted=312
2024-03-06T12:06:41Z INFO routing: chosen variant=llama-70b-q4_0, fallback=opt-13b-gguf
2024-03-06T12:06:42Z ERROR stream: stall_detected session=req-9f7c3b token_idx=148 seq_len=2300
```

samir: that matches. eviction thrash -> per-request KV cache warmup -> streaming stalls -> queues back up. first mitigation thoughts?

maya: we can do two quick actions: 1) route rivermark to their dedicated fallback variant (smaller quantized) to reduce prefix memory pressure, 2) bump worker_count on their dedicated pool by +25% to drain backlog.

sre-lead: do both. apply routing change first (fast). samir, joan, coordinate. keep an eye on p99 and streaming stalls.

joan: running route change now via control-plane CLI:
```
redwood routes set --customer rivermark --from model=llama-70b-q4_0 --to model=opt-13b-gguf --policy temporary-fallback --duration 30m
```

ops-bot: executed: routes update accepted (op-id: op-20240306-33). routing table updated for rivermark.

samir: scaling workers on dedicated pool rivermark-dp:
```
kubectl scale deployment/rivermark-infer --replicas=15 -n dedicated-rivermark
```

ops-bot: HPA/scale triggered. nodes autoscaler requested +2 GPU nodes in eu-west-1 (req: autoscaler-20240306-78).

lee: quick check after route+scale (12:12Z): p95=0.22s p99=1.6s streaming stalls=0.9% active sessions=420. improvement visible in graphs. :thumbsup:

maya: nice. we still need root cause. logs show many unique prompt prefixes (user-supplied long context) causing KV cache fragmentation. hypothesis: rivermark's recent rollout sent long multi-document prompts with small per-request variation, defeating prefix reuse.

samir: agreed. ask rivermark SRE to share recent client changes + sample prompts. I'll open an action item.

joan: also saw a high ratio of requests using streaming+sync combo -> many sessions holding resources while waiting for client acks. flagged in logs: `client-window=0` for some sessions -> they never consumed chunks quickly.

maya: mitigation idea for next deploy: enable prefix canonicalization + increase per-customer KV cache quota. Ops, can we push config change to enable prefix_dedupe for rivermark?

ops-bot: config patch proposed: `customer.rivermark.kv_cache.prefix_dedupe = true` (staged). Applying to dedicated pool in canary (2 pods) now.

sre-lead: good. keep canary until 12:40Z then roll. Also add a short-term rate limit for identical new sessions from same API key to limit fanout.

samir: contacted rivermark on-call (cc'ed) and asked for sample prompts + whether they rolled any client change ~12:00Z. awaiting reply.

joan: saving relevant traces/reqids: req-9f7c3b, req-4a2d11, req-8cbbf0. Uploaded traces to S3: s3://inference-traces/inc-7832/

maya: post-mitigation numbers look stable. marking immediate customer-impact as "degraded" -> now "mitigated". we'll keep as incident until RCA complete.

samir: handing off to day oncall @lee for follow-up RACI and RCA. summary:
- Impact: rivermark single-tenant p99 spike to 11.4s -> mitigated to 1.6s after routing + scale
- Root cause (initial): KV cache fragmentation from high-cardinality long-prefix prompts + client streaming behavior causing resource hold
- Mitigations applied: temporary routing to smaller model, worker scale up, prefix_dedupe canary, short-term rate limit on session creation
- Next actions: collect client prompt samples, complete full RCA, tune kv cache policy and customer quota, consider control-plane validation to avoid high-cardinality prompt fanout

lee: taking handoff. I'll keep this incident open and create a post-incident doc. assigning follow-ups to: samir (customer prompt sample), joan (RAC/kv policy changes), maya (postmortem draft).

ops-bot: created ticket INC-7832 in JIRA: https://jira.example.com/browse/INC-7832

samir: thanks team. good job. :coffee:

joan: adding correlation note: we saw a smaller similar pattern 2024-02-18 but at lower volume; may be a customer-side config/upgrade.

lee: will update channel when RCA PR is ready and when we schedule kv cache tuning. moving to monitoring mode.

incident-bot: Incident INC-7832 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. channel will be updated on closure.
